title: Energy Internet Routing using Quantum Optimization Algorithms
authors: Alireza Alamgir Tehrani, Mehrdad Boroushaki, Abbas Rajabi
abstract: The Energy Internet (EI) is a new concept aimed at enhancing the integration of renewable energy sources with the energy grid. Energy-efficient path selection in EI is NP-hard. This research presents an innovative Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) and Ising Hamiltonian formulation for energy routing. The validation and scalability of the proposed formulation were evaluated by applying quantum-inspired annealing and quantum gate optimization to two case studies, a 9-node and a 30-node EI network. A comparative analysis was presented between classical optimization using the Dijkstra algorithm, optimization-based methods, and QAOA using the Qiskit Sampler Primitive, NumpyEigenSolver, and quantum-inspired annealing using the Ocean exact Solver, D-Wave Tabu Sampler, and D-Wave Simulated Annealing. Simulation results based on the proposed formulation agree with the exact solution, while the runtime of classical approaches is less than that of quantum approaches. However, the Simulated Annealing sampler offers the shortest runtime among all quantum methods.
summary: This research tackles the NP-hard energy routing problem in the Energy Internet by formulating it as a QUBO/Ising model. The authors compare solving this model using classical algorithms (like Dijkstra) against various quantum approaches (QAOA and Quantum Annealing). While the quantum methods validate the formulation, classical solvers demonstrated significantly faster runtime performance on the tested networks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the NP-hard problem of finding the energy-efficient path selection (energy routing) within the Energy Internet (EI).
main_result: While quantum methods successfully formulated the problem, classical algorithms like Dijkstra's showed superior runtime performance for the tested 9-node and 30-node networks.
method: The problem is mapped onto a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) and Ising Hamiltonian, which are then solved using comparative quantum and classical optimization techniques.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the Energy Internet (EI), a network integrating renewable energy sources and loads. The core mathematical tool is the QUBO/Ising formulation derived from minimizing total energy losses (router and conduction losses).
key_observables: Optimal routing path, total energy losses (W), and computational time (s).
important_parameters: Network size (9-node and 30-node), transmission power (1 kW), and quantum circuit depth (p=1 for QAOA).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes treating power transmission as a constant parameter to linearize the non-linear loss function for QUBO formulation; quantum simulations are run on classical hardware.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the EI components and the 9-node network graph structure; Tables compare the performance metrics (time, loss) across Dijkstra, QAOA, and quantum-inspired annealing for both 9-node and 30-node cases.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the EI routing problem and its NP-hard nature. It then develops the QUBO/Ising formulation by incorporating loss functions and constraints. Finally, it compares the performance of classical solvers (Dijkstra) against quantum approaches (QAOA, Quantum Annealing) on increasing network sizes.
why_interesting: The work demonstrates a direct application of quantum optimization techniques (QUBO/Ising) to a complex, real-world engineering problem, providing a benchmark for quantum computation feasibility in infrastructure management.
